methodology: DeepMind-style DIRECT verification: frozen challenge + labeled solution + independent evaluator (the FunSearch/AlphaCode challenge/solution/evaluator grading pattern). No Lean in this lane; the evaluator re-derives every machine-checkable claim from scratch with exact integer arithmetic.

statement_frozen.corpus_verbatim: Let $f(n)$ be minimal such that any $f(n)$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, no three on a line, contain $n$ points which form the vertices of a convex $n$-gon. Prove that $f(n)=2^{n-2}+1$. [#107, prize $500]
statement_frozen.task_elaboration: The Erdos-Klein-Szekeres Happy Ending problem. f(n) = the smallest number of points in general position (no 3 collinear) in the plane such that any such set contains n points in convex position (vertices of a convex n-gon). Known: f(3)=3, f(4)=5 (Klein 1931), f(5)=9 (Turan-Makai/Erdos-Szekeres), f(6)=17 (Szekeres-Peters computer-assisted 2006); bounds 2^{n-2}+1 <= f(n) <= 2^{n+O(sqrt(n log n))} (HMPT20); conjecture f(n) = 2^{n-2}+1. Prize context: Erdos $500 for proof / $100 for disproof; Graham $1000 for proof.
statement_frozen.corpus_context: The problem originated in 1931 when Klein observed that f(4)=5. Turan and Makai showed f(5)=9. Erdos and Szekeres proved the bounds 2^{n-2}+1 <= f(n) <= binom(2n-4, n-2)+1 (ErSz60 / ErSz35). Improvements of the upper bound (all 4^{(1+o(1))n}) until Suk [Su17]: f(n) <= 2^{(1+o(1))n}; current best HMPT20: f(n) <= 2^{n+O(sqrt(n log n))}.

conventions_pinned.general_position: A finite point set S is in general position (GP) iff no three points of S are collinear. Machine predicate: for every triple (P,Q,R) of distinct points, orient(P,Q,R) != 0, where orient(P,Q,R) := (Q-P) x (R-P) is the planar cross product (the campaign convention, PROOF.md section 0). Three points CAN be collinear in arbitrary sets; such sets simply violate GP and are outside the quantifier of f(n).
conventions_pinned.integer_universe: The comparator's finite universe: point sets are finite sets of integer coordinate pairs (x,y) in Z^2. The mathematical problem lives in R^2; every machine certificate below is exact over Z^2 (cross-product sign tests, exact integers, Fractions only where algebraically exact; NO floats in any geometric predicate). Exhaustive checks are exhaustive over the stated integer grids; randomized checks sample Z^2 boxes. This pins the campaign's witness convention (PROOF.md section 0 and engine107.py witnesses: all integer coordinates).
conventions_pinned.convex_position: A finite set S (|S| = n >= 3) is in convex position iff every point of S is a vertex (extreme point) of conv(S), i.e., no point of S lies in conv(S \ {p}). Under GP this is equivalent to: no point lies in the closed triangle of three others (Caratheodory in R^2; on-segment cases need collinearity, excluded by GP). A set of n points in convex position is the vertex set of a convex n-gon.
conventions_pinned.cup_cap: A k-cup is a set of k points with pairwise distinct x-coordinates which, x-sorted, has strictly increasing successive segment slopes; a k-cap: strictly decreasing (PROOF.md section 0). Slopes compared as exact Fractions.
conventions_pinned.f_definition: f(n) = min N such that EVERY N-point GP set contains n points in convex position. Equivalently: f(n) > m iff there EXISTS an m-point GP set with no n points in convex position.

acceptance_criteria.claim: f(3)=3 both directions on the finite universe
acceptance_criteria.machine_check: (i) a 2-point GP set exists with no convex 3-subset (vacuous subset sweep); (ii) EVERY GP 3-subset of the 4x4 and 5x5 grids and random samples is in convex position by BOTH checker methods; (iii) collinear triples exist, are rejected by the GP gate, and are rejected by both convexity methods (the convention is encoded).

regenerate the 4-point witness (3 hull + 1 strict interior); verify GP (all 4 triples), verify NO 4-subset in convex position (the unique 4-subset fails), identify the interior point by exact triangle containment; grid census: GP 4-subsets not in convex position exist in both grids.

>= 10^4 random GP 5-point sets (uniform box) + adversarial structured sets + EXHAUSTIVE all GP 5-subsets of the 4x4 and 5x5 grids: every one contains a convex 4-subset (all C(5,4)=5 subsets tested by the two-method integer checker). Zero failures required; grid sweeps must be non-vacuous (count > 0).

regenerate the five 8-point witnesses (four 5x5-lattice sets + the interleaved cup/cap family); each: GP + ALL C(8,5)=56 subsets have NO convex 5-gon (two-method checker); at least 3 distinct witnesses required; PLUS an independent re-derivation sweep (all 4-column x 2-point subsets of the 5x5 grid) that must rediscover >= 3 witnesses including the four known lattice ones; PLUS 9-point GP extensions of every witness must contain a convex 5-subset (corroborates the cited f(5)=9 upper side on these instances).

the two independent convex-position methods (angular tour around the centroid with integer direction vectors; exhaustive closed-triangle containment) must agree on EVERY query across all parts (tens of thousands of queries, mixed true/false, sizes 3..8, degenerate controls included); zero disagreements required.

for every (a,b) with a,b >= 2 and (a-1)(b-1)+1 <= 8: EVERY order type (permutation of [1..L], L=(a-1)(b-1)+1) contains an a-increasing or b-decreasing subsequence; the block construction of length (a-1)(b-1) has neither (tightness); random distinct-value sequences corroborate.

corrupted witnesses (single point moved by unit vectors) must produce convex 5-gons in the overwhelming majority of GP-preserving corruptions (measured rate printed; threshold enforced); collinear triples (several slopes) must be rejected by the GP gate with the offending triple identified; non-GP sets must be rejected by the sweep gate; a known convex pentagon must be detected (positive control).

verdict_protocol: The evaluator prints per-part receipts (CMP107-A..CMP107-I, CMP107-Z3) and the final line COMPARATOR_107_GREEN=1 iff every gate passes; exit code 0 on green, nonzero on any failure. CI job kernel-107cmp greps the receipts and echoes KERNEL107CMP_GREEN=1.

fetched_urls.facts: AlphaGeometry (Nature, January 2024): neuro-symbolic system (language model guiding a symbolic deduction engine); solved 25 of 30 IMO-AG-30 olympiad geometry problems (2000-2022) under competition time limits; previous state-of-the-art solved 10; average human gold medalist solved 25.9. Trained on 100M synthetic proofs, no human demonstrations. Evan Chen: output 'both verifiable and clean'.
The Nature paper 'Solving olympiad geometry without human demonstrations' (Trinh et al., 2024) — the AlphaGeometry primary source.

IMO 2024 (published July 25, 2024): AlphaProof (reinforcement-learning system proving in the formal language Lean; proofs formally verified) + AlphaGeometry 2 solved 4 of 6 IMO 2024 problems, 28/42 points, silver-medal standard (gold threshold 29). AlphaGeometry 2 solved 83% of all historical IMO geometry problems from the past 25 years, vs 53% for its predecessor; AG2 solved IMO 2024 Problem 4 within 19 seconds after formalization. Solutions scored by Prof Sir Timothy Gowers and Dr Joseph Myers under IMO rules.

IMO 2025 (published July 21, 2025): an advanced version of Gemini with Deep Think solved 5 of 6 problems perfectly, 35/42 points — officially a gold-medal standard score, graded and certified by IMO coordinators under the same criteria as student solutions; end-to-end natural language; DeepMind states it continues progress on its formal systems AlphaGeometry and AlphaProof (verified reasoning in formal languages).

FunSearch (Nature, December 2023): pairs a pre-trained LLM proposing creative solutions as computer code with an automated EVALUATOR that guards against hallucinations — the challenge/solution/evaluator grading pattern this comparator adopts.
AlphaProof Code: DeepMind's formal-verification positioning — agents generating millions of lines of Lean to mathematically prove code accuracy (AlphaProof's Lean-based lineage).

honest_positioning: DeepMind's public systems solve OLYMPIAD GEOMETRY synthetically (AlphaGeometry: IMO-AG-30 25/30; AlphaGeometry 2: 83% of historical IMO geometry) and reached IMO gold standard at IMO 2025 with Gemini Deep Think (35/42).

The Happy Ending problem (#107) is a combinatorial-geometry EXTREMAL problem (an open research problem of Erdos with prize money), NOT in DeepMind's solved set; the conjecture f(n) = 2^{n-2}+1 remains OPEN for n >= 7 and no DeepMind system has announced anything toward it.

This comparator does NOT use DeepMind solvers. It uses their DIRECT-verification methodology: a frozen challenge, a labeled solution, and an independent automated evaluator that directly checks every machine-checkable claim (the FunSearch/AlphaCode grading pattern).
The campaign's Lean/AlphaProof-style formalization lane for #107 is separate (kernel lanes); this lane is python-only with exact integer arithmetic.
